the flow rate is a non-Gaussian random variable with a mean and a standard deviation that are both significantly greater than the mean and standard deviation of the permeability field, and that the downstream exit-point is a non-Gaussion random variable whose mean is greater and whose variance is less than the mean and variance of the permeability.

(a) the flow rate and drawdown statistics are strongly dependent on the spatial correlation of the soil permeability; and (b) the exit-point statistics are strongly dependent both on the soil permeability correlation and on the dam height.

(1) the mean flow rate through an earth dam with spatially random permeability is less than through a deterministic dam; and (2) the variance of flow through a dam with random permeability is greater than that through a deterministic dam.
